set.typical_award_size: The County applied for Homekey+ in 2025 with Restorative Partners for the Healing and Restoration Campus (HARC) on Los Osos Valley Road, permanent supportive housing for justice-involved people at risk of homelessness; the County's 2025 year-end report (dated March 10, 2026) says no Homekey+ award notice had been received, and no San Luis Obispo County project appears on HCD's Homekey+ awardee list as of October 13, 2026 (statewide total awarded about $1.03 billion of the $2.2 billion Proposition 1 allocation). Separately the County is advancing Welcome Home Village (40 permanent supportive housing units and 14 interim shelter units, anticipated opening spring 2026). The County's FY 2025/26 contracts for services, affordable housing and public facilities totaled $13,646,539.60. Earlier Homekey: City of San Luis Obispo Calle Joaquin (76 units, $19.4 million Homekey plus $2.6 million County SB 1090; not re-verified in the audit).
set.cycle_notes: HCD Homekey+ accepts applications for all project types continuously until funds are exhausted (NOFA November 26, 2024, amended January 31, 2025, August 7, 2025 and March 27, 2026); a pre-application consultation with HCD is required. The County's HARC application had no award on the October 13, 2026 awardee list.
set.next_deadline: Rolling until Homekey+ funds are exhausted; HCD shows the application portal open as of November 8, 2026. Welcome Home Village financing is County-led; contact HSD for partnership opportunities.
set.audit_note: Prior text said Homekey+ funds were fully committed statewide; HCD's Homekey+ and Timeline pages show continuous applications and an open portal, so cycle changed from closed/inactive to rolling. Calle Joaquin figures not re-verified.

reason: County report confirms the HARC application, Welcome Home Village and contract total, but HCD shows Homekey+ still accepting applications on a rolling basis rather than fully committed.

set.typical_award_size: Gap grants and below-market loans at Council discretion under adopted criteria (Resolution 9263, 2001 Series). Housing Element history: $10,450,954 of in-lieu funds granted, loaned or committed to 464 deed-restricted units since the 1999 inclusionary ordinance; Bishop Street Studios (34 units) received $1,595,500 combined AHF loan, impact fee deferral loan and CDBG loan; $330,000 grant to TMHA for a 6-unit acquisition-rehab. Not confirmed on an agency source in the audit: a $2 million January 2020 approval for a 108-unit project; a 2023 Council resolution approving $3.2 million to HASLO for 736 Orcutt Road ($2.0 million) and 279 Bridge Street ($1.2 million); and $750,000 of 2024 Prohousing Incentive funds routed through the AHF. Housing Element target: support at least 4 new affordable developments during the planning period.
set.audit_note: Core program facts (Program 2.5, Res. 9263 criteria, grant and below-market loan use, ELI through moderate income, 55/45 year terms, $10.45M history) confirmed in the HCD-hosted Housing Element; post-2020 award figures could not be confirmed because slocity.org returns 403.

reason: Housing Element supports award type, income levels, terms and the Council award process; post-2020 award figures are not in the source and are now labeled unconfirmed.

Housing Element incentives table confirms the full development services fee exemption for ELI, VLI and low income projects, the per-unit waiver for mixed-income projects, and the impact fee deferral criteria.

set.typical_award_size: Case-by-case Council approval of long-term deferral of City water connection, sewer connection, development impact and building permit fees, structured as General Fund loans repaid several years beyond occupancy. Oak Park Public Housing (Paso Robles Housing Authority) phases one through four received fee deferral loans of $1.018 million (Resolution 12-031), $889,000 (14-019), $999,423 (17-019) and $1,438,160.71 (Resolution 18-020, 2018). Resolution 18-020 terms: promissory note repaid over up to 30 years from building permit at 3.75% simple interest from residual receipts, secured by a deed of trust. News reports (not agency sources) describe a March 2026 Council resolution deferring water, sewer, development impact and building permit fees for affordable housing, a 30-year deferral of about $1.2 million for Highland's Senior Affordable Apartments (298 Niblick Road), a 30-year deferral of about $1.8 million for Sunrise Villas Apartments, a roughly 50% impact fee waiver for a nine-unit Habitat for Humanity project on Vine Street, and February 2021 deferrals for a 79-unit senior project at Woodland Plaza II.
set.affordability_requirement: Units affordable to lower-income households (Health and Safety Code 50079.5), including extremely low income; City practice requires a recorded affordability covenant for the longest feasible time and not less than 30 years (Resolution 18-020).
set.next_deadline: Rolling; no open round or deadline as of November 8, 2026. Requests go to Council with the entitlement or before building permit; contact Community Development at (805) 237-3970 or planning@prcity.com.
set.cycle_notes: No NOFA. Housing Element Program 7 (Affordable Housing Support) commits the City to offer impact fee deferrals for lower-income units and allow deferral of fees several years beyond occupancy; each deferral is approved by Council resolution.
